issue.title: Extend the workspace-exclusivity guarantee to the sase-github plugin
issue.description: The sase-github plugin acquires workspaces the same way the rest of SASE does: every gh__setup and GitHub-submit allocation is a single atomic claim whose result is checked and whose ledger record names its caller, a pinned n=<num> target that a live agent holds fails with that agent named instead of being taken, and no gh workflow step stashes, pulls, or checks out inside a checkout another live agent occupies.

issue.title: Atomic, checked workspace acquisition in the sase-github plugin
issue.description: gh_atomic: replace the check-then-claim allocation in gh__setup and in the GitHub submit path with a single atomic claim, check every claim result, make a pinned n=<num> target a single-shot claim that names the occupant on failure, release the slot when materialization fails, and give every claim and release a caller tag.

issue.title: Refuse gh workflow steps that would prepare an occupied checkout
issue.description: gh_guard: write the per-checkout occupant record when gh__setup takes a workspace, clear it on release, and require the occupancy decision before gh__prepare stashes, gh__checkout checks out, or the GitHub submit path checks out, so a conflicting occupant fails the run instead of losing another agent's work.

payload.entry: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: sase just check fails on pre-existing toobig — tests/_suite_gate.py is 1197 lines on current master (limit 1000); unrelated to the sase-github claim rewrite and not caused by this phase.

Atomic, checked claims in sase-github: gh__setup unpinned path uses claim_next_axe_workspace then ensure_workspace_checkout/materialize_sdd_store (releases the slot if either raises); pinned n=<num> is a single-shot claim_workspace that names the live occupant and exits 1 without materializing; claim results are never discarded; pre_allocated still skips claiming; ws_submit uses claim_next_axe_workspace_dir + finally release; caller tags are gh-setup / gh-submit / gh-release. Verified: sase-github just check 211 passed (atomic skip, release-on-fail, pinned occupant, submit finally, ledger tags); sase plugin consumer tests 34 passed; setup_required_plugins installs the local checkout; occupancy_conflicts doctor OK; no --epic-symbol leftovers. sase just check itself failed on pre-existing toobig (tests/_suite_gate.py).

Atomic, checked claims in sase-github: gh__setup unpinned path uses claim_next_axe_workspace then ensure_workspace_checkout/materialize_sdd_store (releases the slot if either raises); pinned n=<num> is a single-shot claim_workspace that names the live occupant and exits 1 without materializing; claim results are never discarded; pre_allocated still skips claiming; ws_submit uses claim_next_axe_workspace_dir + finally release; caller tags are gh-setup / gh-submit / gh-release. Verified: sase-github just check 211 passed (atomic skip, release-on-fail, pinned occupant, submit finally, ledger tags); sase plugin consumer tests 34 passed; setup_required_plugins installs the local checkout; occupancy_conflicts doctor OK; no --epic-symbol leftovers. sase just check itself failed on pre-existing toobig (tests/_suite_gate.py).

gh_guard implemented in sase-github: gh_setup.py writes .sase/occupant.json for real numbered workspaces (workspace_num > 1, matching run_agent_phases.py's convention) and calls ensure_workspace_not_occupied before handing the checkout to prepare/checkout, on both the claimed and pre_allocated branches; ws_submit_changespec guards the submit checkout before provider.checkout(); gh.yml's release step clears the occupant record via clear_occupant_record(setup.workspace_dir) alongside the existing gh-release caller tag. Verified: rebuilt sase_core_rs locally (maturin develop --release against linked sase-core, since the installed wheel predated decide_workspace_occupant_conflict); full sase-github suite (219 tests, including 20 in test_gh_workspace_claims.py covering occupant-record writes, refusal on a live rival occupant, proceeding when the occupant is self or a dead pid, and the submit-path refusal) all pass; ruff check and mypy clean; no epic-symbol leftovers (sase bead epic-symbols reported none); sase doctor --check workspace.occupancy_conflicts OK.

LANDING (sase-q0.5.land): epic complete and closed. Verified both phases against the source and their commits in the sase-github linked repo (both pushed, origin/master in sync).

VERIFIED (read the code and the commits, not just the phase notes):
- sase-q0.5.1 / 61dd36f "feat: claim GitHub workspaces atomically" — gh_setup.py's unpinned branch now calls claim_next_axe_workspace(caller_tag="gh-setup") first and materializes second via _materialize_or_release, which release_workspace()es the slot when ensure_workspace_checkout or materialize_sdd_store raises. The pinned n=<num> branch is a single-shot claim_workspace whose result IS checked; on failure it prints the occupant (name, pid, liveness, workflow, artifacts timestamp, via _describe_workspace_occupant/_format_workspace_occupant copied from run_agent_phases.py) to stderr and sys.exit(1) without materializing. No claim result is discarded on any branch. The pre_allocated branch is untouched, as the plan required. workspace_plugin.ws_submit_changespec was converted to claim_next_axe_workspace_dir(..., caller_tag="gh-submit") inside try/except WorkspaceClaimError, dropping the get_first_available_axe_workspace + get_workspace_directory_for_num + claim_workspace trio, and its finally: release_workspace now carries caller_tag="gh-submit". gh.yml's release step carries caller_tag="gh-release".
- sase-q0.5.2 / 51347d4 "feat(workspace): guard gh workflow steps against occupied checkouts" — gh_setup.py writes .sase/occupant.json via new_occupant_record/write_occupant_record for real numbered workspaces only (workspace_num > 1, matching claim_deferred_workspace's guard), and calls ensure_workspace_not_occupied before printing _chdir, on the claimed and pre_allocated branches alike, so one guard covers gh__prepare's `git stash push --include-untracked` and gh__checkout's provider.checkout, which both run in that directory immediately afterwards. ws_submit_changespec guards ws_dir before provider.checkout(); its refusal returns (False, "Refusing checkout: ...") from inside the try, so the finally still releases. gh.yml's release step calls clear_occupant_record(setup.workspace_dir).
- Confirmed the pre_allocated pid identity the guard depends on: claim_deferred_workspace writes the RUNNING row and the occupant record with os.getpid() of the axe runner; run_execution_loop calls execute_workflow in that same process, and _execute_python_step runs each step as a direct child, so gh_setup's os.getppid() is that same pid and decide_workspace_occupant_conflict's pid comparison recognises the caller's own lineage instead of refusing every pre-allocated #gh run.
- Confirmed the occupant record gh_setup writes is reachable by the rest of the system: the plugin's ws_get_workspace_directory hook resolves through the same ensure_workspace_checkout(primary_workspace_dir, num), so stale_running_cleanup._clear_stale_occupant_record and the workspace.occupancy_conflicts doctor check resolve to the same directory. `sase doctor --check workspace.occupancy_conflicts` is OK.
- Swept the plugin for leftovers: no get_first_available_* callers remain, no unchecked claim results, no unguarded destructive prep.

FIXED DURING LANDING (99a6277, this epic's own defect): gh_setup claims before it guards, so a WorkspaceOccupiedError left the RUNNING row held — a failed `setup` step means gh.yml's `release` step never runs, because its `if: {{ setup.should_release }}` condition cannot evaluate once setup's outputs are missing, so the slot stayed claimed for the lifetime of the executor process until stale-claim cleanup reaped it. The guard call is now wrapped so a refusal releases the slot it just claimed, mirroring _materialize_or_release; the pre_allocated branch releases nothing, since the launcher owns that claim. Two regression tests added (test_setup_releases_its_claim_when_the_guard_refuses, which fails without the fix, and test_pre_allocated_guard_refusal_releases_nothing).

INTEGRATION (commits since this epic's first commit 61dd36f, excluding its own): sase-github had none. sase-core had none since 35c09db. The sase repo landed five, of which two touch this epic's surface and neither needed an edit here: 893fb2352 split running_field/_operations.py into per-operation modules — verbatim moves behind the same sase.running_field facade, so every name gh_setup.py and workspace_plugin.py import (claim_workspace, claim_next_axe_workspace, claim_next_axe_workspace_dir, release_workspace, get_claimed_workspaces, WorkspaceClaim, WorkspaceClaimError, ClaimResult) still resolves; 7563372f1 added the same ensure_workspace_not_occupied guard to prepare_opened_checkout for `workspace open --clean` (task sase-qc), which complements rather than duplicates this epic. No sase-repo docs name the gh call sites or the caller tags, so nothing there went stale.

VERIFICATION: sase-github suite 221 passed (was 219 before the landing fix), ruff check clean, ruff format clean, mypy clean — all run with the sase workspace venv after `just install`, which builds sase_core_rs from the linked sase-core checkout (decide_workspace_occupant_conflict present) and installs sase-github editable as a required plugin. sase repo: tests/test_core_occupancy_guard.py + tests/test_running_field_operations.py + tests/main/test_workspace_open_clean_occupancy.py + tests/test_axe_chop_plugins_required.py + tests/test_plugin_catalog.py, 68 passed. `just symvision` green; `sase bead epic-symbols` reports no entries for sase-q0.5 or sase-q0.
